citation: IRS Pub. 1345 (Rev. 12-2025), Reporting of Security Incidents (N54-R03)
trigger: Any event that can result in unauthorized disclosure, misuse, modification, or destruction of taxpayer information. Clock starts at confirmation of the incident
deadline: As soon as possible but not later than the next business day after confirmation
notify: IRS. An ERO-only provider contacts its local Stakeholder Liaison, following the Data Theft Information for Tax Professionals instructions
applies_at_this_tier: Yes. The firm is an Authorized IRS e-file Provider (ERO) for individual returns. Tax Partner (Responsible Official) calls

citation: IRS Data Theft Information for Tax Professionals (guidance, not a regulation) (N54-R03)
trigger: Client data stolen or accessed by an unauthorized person
deadline: As quickly as possible ('Speed is critical'). In practice the same call as the Pub. 1345 report
notify: Local IRS Stakeholder Liaison, who notifies IRS Criminal Investigation and others in the IRS. IRS toll-free assisters cannot take third-party identity theft reports
applies_at_this_tier: Yes

citation: IRS Data Theft Information for Tax Professionals (guidance)
trigger: Data theft affecting clients for whom the firm prepares state returns
deadline: As quickly as possible, alongside the IRS report
notify: Each state tax agency where the firm prepares returns, using the Federation of Tax Administrators 'Report a Data Breach' contact list
applies_at_this_tier: Yes. Florida has no personal income tax; notify the agencies of the other states where affected clients file

citation: IRS Data Theft Information for Tax Professionals (guidance)
trigger: Data theft; attempted or completed refund diversion
deadline: As soon as possible after declaration
notify: FBI local field office; Secret Service local office if directed; local police report
applies_at_this_tier: Yes. Needed for the Florida no-harm consultation (501.171(4)(c)) if that path is considered

trigger: Acquisition of unencrypted customer information of at least 500 consumers without authorization. Unauthorized access is presumed to be acquisition unless reliable evidence shows otherwise (314.2(m)). Clock starts on discovery: the first day the event is known to any employee, officer, or other agent other than the attacker (314.4(j)(2))
deadline: As soon as possible, and no later than 30 days after discovery
notify: FTC, electronically on the form at ftc.gov. Content: firm name and contact; types of information; date or date range; number of consumers; general description; any written law enforcement determination and contact (314.4(j)(1)(i)-(vi))
applies_at_this_tier: Yes if 500 or more consumers. The 314.6 exception does not remove (j). Count consumers (individual clients), not business entities

trigger: A law enforcement official gives a written determination that notifying the public would impede a criminal investigation or damage national security
deadline: The official may request an initial delay of up to 30 days after the FTC notice, extendable by up to 60 days on written request
notify: Include the determination and the official's contact in the FTC notice
applies_at_this_tier: If requested. It delays public disclosure by the FTC, not the firm's 30-day filing

trigger: Breach of security: unauthorized access of electronic personal information. Includes name with SSN; name with a financial account number and any required access code; and an email address or user name with a password (a BEC mailbox credential itself counts)
deadline: As expeditiously as practicable and without unreasonable delay, and no later than 30 days after determination of the breach or reason to believe a breach occurred
notify: Each affected Florida resident, by mail or email. Content: date or date range, description of the information, and firm contact information
applies_at_this_tier: Yes

obligation: Florida notice to the Department of Legal Affairs
trigger: Breach affecting 500 or more individuals in Florida
deadline: As expeditiously as practicable, no later than 30 days after determination. 15 more days if good cause is given in writing within the 30 days
notify: Department of Legal Affairs (Attorney General). Content: synopsis, number of Floridians, free services offered, copy of the individual notice, firm contact
applies_at_this_tier: Yes if 500 or more Florida residents

obligation: Florida notice to consumer reporting agencies
trigger: Notice required to more than 1,000 individuals at a single time
deadline: Without unreasonable delay
notify: All nationwide consumer reporting agencies: timing, distribution, and content of the notices
applies_at_this_tier: Yes if more than 1,000

trigger: After investigation and consultation with law enforcement, the firm reasonably determines the breach has not and will not likely result in identity theft or other financial harm
deadline: Written determination kept 5 years; copy to the Department within 30 days after the determination
notify: Department of Legal Affairs
applies_at_this_tier: Unlikely for this incident type: stolen tax documents are used for refund fraud. Counsel decides

trigger: A law enforcement agency determines individual notice would interfere with a criminal investigation
deadline: Delay for the period in the agency's written request
notify: Hold individual notices; keep the written request
applies_at_this_tier: If requested

trigger: Notice given under the rules of the firm's primary or functional federal regulator
deadline: Deemed compliant if the firm notifies individuals under those rules and timely gives the Department a copy
notify: n/a
applies_at_this_tier: No for this firm. The FTC Safeguards Rule requires notice to the FTC only, not to individuals, so there is no federal individual notice to rely on. Florida individual and Department notices must be sent. Counsel confirms

obligation: Service provider breach notice to the firm (inbound)
trigger: A breach of a system maintained by a third-party agent (for example the tax software, portal, or cloud provider)
deadline: Agent notifies the firm as expeditiously as practicable, no later than 10 days after determination
notify: The firm, which then gives the (3) and (4) notices
applies_at_this_tier: Yes. Track in contracts (314.4(f)(2); POAM-010)

trigger: Affected individuals who reside outside Florida (about 9% of individual clients live elsewhere for part or all of the year)
deadline: Varies by state
notify: Residents, and state attorneys general or regulators where each state requires
applies_at_this_tier: Yes. Apply the law of each state where affected individuals reside; counsel builds the list from the client addresses

citation: IRS Data Theft Information for Tax Professionals (guidance)
trigger: Client data theft
deadline: Work with law enforcement on timing; combine with the Florida and other state notices
notify: Individual letter to each victim. Clients file Form 14039 only if they receive an IRS notice or their e-filed return is rejected for a duplicate SSN
applies_at_this_tier: Yes

trigger: Suspected security incident
deadline: Per policy. Call the carrier breach hotline before hiring vendors
notify: Carrier breach hotline
applies_at_this_tier: Yes. Contractual, not legal

obligation: Business associate breach notice to covered entity
trigger: Breach of unsecured PHI held for a covered entity
deadline: Without unreasonable delay, no later than 60 calendar days after discovery
notify: HIPAA covered entity client
applies_at_this_tier: No. The firm is not a business associate (scenario facts section 1)

trigger: Cyber incident affecting covered defense information
deadline: Within 72 hours of discovery
notify: DoD via https://dibnet.dod.mil
applies_at_this_tier: No. The firm has no federal contracts or subcontracts

obligation: CIRCIA covered cyber incident and ransom payment reports
trigger: Covered cyber incident or ransom payment
deadline: Proposed: 72 hours (incident); 24 hours after ransom payment
notify: CISA
applies_at_this_tier: No. Final rule not published as of 2026-09-25. The firm is also below its SBA size standard, the proposed size criterion

obligation: OFAC sanctions check before any extortion payment
citation: OFAC Updated Advisory on Potential Sanctions Risks for Facilitating Ransomware Payments (Sept. 21, 2021); 31 CFR ch. V
trigger: An extortion demand is considered for payment (not typical of BEC)
deadline: Before any payment. Full and timely reporting to law enforcement is a mitigating factor
notify: OFAC; FBI
applies_at_this_tier: Only if an extortion demand arises (POL-03 4.8)
